subtopic: Ratio of Areas of Two Triangles
stem: In the following figure, seg BE \(\perp\) seg AB and seg BA \(\perp\) seg AD. If BE = 6 and AD = 9, find \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ABE)}{A(\triangle BAD)}\).
solution: \(\triangle ABE\) and \(\triangle BAD\) have the same base AB. Areas of triangles with a common base are in the ratio of their corresponding heights. Here BE and AD are the heights on the common base AB. Hence \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ABE)}{A(\triangle BAD)} = \dfrac{BE}{AD} = \dfrac{6}{9} = \dfrac{2}{3}\).
figureNote: figure with seg BE perpendicular to AB at B and seg BA perpendicular to AD at A; E and B along the top, A and D along the bottom, p-00

stem: If two circles with radii 8 cm and 3 cm respectively touch internally, then find the distance between their centres.
solution: When two circles touch each other internally, the distance between their centres is equal to the difference of their radii. Distance between the centres \(= 8 - 3 = 5\) cm.

stem: Find the height of an equilateral triangle whose side is 6 units.
solution: Height of an equilateral triangle \(= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times \text{side} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times 6 = 3\sqrt{3}\) units.

stem: If the angle \(\theta = -45^\circ\), find the value of \(\tan\theta\).
Find the slope and \(y\)-intercept of the line \(y = 3x - 5\).
solution: Comparing the given line \(y = 3x - 5\) with \(y = mx + c\), where \(m\) is the slope and \(c\) is the \(y\)-intercept. Hence slope \(m = 3\) and \(y\)-intercept \(c = -5\).

stem: Find the circumference of a circle whose radius is 7 cm.
solution: Circumference of a circle \(= 2\pi r = 2\times \dfrac{22}{7}\times 7 = 44\) cm.

subtopic: Property of an Angle Bisector of a Triangle
stem: In \(\triangle PQR\), seg RS is the bisector of \(\angle PRQ\). If PS = 6, SQ = 8 and PR = 12, find QR.
solution: By the angle bisector theorem, the bisector RS divides the opposite side PQ in the ratio of the sides containing the angle: \(\dfrac{PR}{QR} = \dfrac{PS}{SQ}\). Putting PS = 6, SQ = 8, PR = 12: \(\dfrac{12}{QR} = \dfrac{6}{8}\), so \(QR = 12\times \dfrac{8}{6} = 16\) units.
figureNote: triangle PQR with vertex P at top, Q and R at the base; cevian RS drawn from R to point S on side PQ, with two arc marks at R showing the bisected angle, p-01

stem: In the given figure, two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at the point P. If PA = 10, PB = 2 and PC = 5, find PD.
solution: For two chords of a circle intersecting inside the circle at P, \(PA\times PB = PC\times PD\). Putting PA = 10, PB = 2, PC = 5: \(10\times 2 = 5\times PD\), so \(PD = \dfrac{10\times 2}{5} = 4\) units.
figureNote: circle with two chords AB and CD intersecting at interior point P; C and B on the upper part of the circle, A and D on the lower part, p-01

stem: Draw \(\angle ABC\) of measure \(135^\circ\) and bisect it.
solution: Steps of construction: (1) Draw ray BC. (2) At B, using a protractor, draw \(\angle ABC = 135^\circ\) to get ray BA. (3) With B as centre and a convenient radius, draw an arc cutting ray BA and ray BC. (4) From these two points of intersection, with equal radii draw two arcs meeting at point D inside the angle. (5) Draw ray BD. Ray BD is the required bisector, with \(\angle ABD = \angle DBC = 67.5^\circ\).

stem: Find the sine ratio of \(\theta\) in standard position whose terminal arm passes through \((3, 4)\).
solution: Here \(x = 3\) and \(y = 4\). \(r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{25} = 5\) units. Hence \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{y}{r} = \dfrac{4}{5}\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: The dimensions of a cuboid in cm are \(50 \times 18 \times 10\). Find its volume.
solution: Volume of cuboid \(= l\times b\times h = 50\times 18\times 10 = 9000\) cm\(^3\).

stem: Prove that: If the angles of a triangle are \(45^\circ - 45^\circ - 90^\circ\), then each of the perpendicular sides is \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) times the hypotenuse.
solution:
Given: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A = \angle C = 45^\circ\) and \(\angle B = 90^\circ\). To prove: \(AB = BC = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}AC\).
Proof: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A = \angle C = 45^\circ\), so the sides opposite to the congruent angles are equal, i.e. \(AB = BC\) ...(i). By Pythagoras theorem, \(AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2\). From (i), \(AC^2 = AB^2 + AB^2 = 2AB^2\), so \(\dfrac{1}{2}AC^2 = AB^2\). Taking square roots, \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}AC = AB\). Hence \(AB = BC = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}AC\).

subtopic: Tangent and Secant to a Circle
stem: Find the angle between the two radii at the centre of the circle as shown in the figure. Lines PA and PB are tangents to the circle at the other ends A and B of the radii OA and OB, and \(\angle APR = 140^\circ\).
solution: \(\angle APR + \angle APB = 180^\circ\) (linear pair). So \(140^\circ + \angle APB = 180^\circ\), giving \(\angle APB = 40^\circ\). Consider quadrilateral OAPB. \(\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ\) (radius is perpendicular to the tangent). Since the sum of the angles of a quadrilateral is \(360^\circ\), \(\angle APB + \angle AOB = 180^\circ\). So \(40^\circ + \angle AOB = 180^\circ\), giving \(\angle AOB = 140^\circ\). The angle between the two radii at the centre of the circle is \(140^\circ\).
figureNote: circle with centre O; tangents PA and PB from external point P touch the circle at A and B; radii OA and OB drawn; a line RPS passes through P with the angle 140 degrees marked at P (angle APR), p-02

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Construct tangents to a circle having radius 3.2 cm and centre 'C', from a point B which is at a distance 7.6 cm from the centre.
solution: Steps of construction: (1) Draw a circle with centre C and radius 3.2 cm. (2) Take a point B such that CB = 7.6 cm. (3) Draw the perpendicular bisector of seg CB and mark its midpoint M. (4) With M as centre and radius MC (= MB), draw a semicircle. (5) Let A be a point of intersection of this semicircle and the given circle. (6) Draw line BA. Line BA is the required tangent (\(\angle CAB = 90^\circ\), as A lies on the semicircle with diameter CB).

stem: From the top of a lighthouse, an observer looks at a ship and finds the angle of depression to be \(60^\circ\). If the height of the lighthouse is 90 metres, then find how far the ship is from the lighthouse. \((\sqrt{3} = 1.73)\)
solution: Let AB be the height of the lighthouse, so AB = 90 m, and let C be the position of the ship with \(\angle ACB = 60^\circ\) (alternate angle to the angle of depression). \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{BC}\), so \(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{90}{BC}\), giving \(BC = \dfrac{90}{\sqrt{3}} = 30\sqrt{3} = 30\times 1.73 = 51.9\) m. The ship is 51.9 m away from the lighthouse.

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: The volume of a cube is \(343\) cm\(^3\). Find its total surface area.
solution: Volume of cube \(= a^3 = 343 = 7^3\), so side \(a = 7\) cm. Total surface area of a cube \(= 6a^2 = 6\times 7\times 7 = 294\) cm\(^2\).

stem: Prove that "The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary".
solution:
Given: \(\square ABCD\) is a cyclic quadrilateral. To prove: \(\angle BAD + \angle BCD = 180^\circ\) and \(\angle ABC + \angle ADC = 180^\circ\).
Proof: Arc BCD is intercepted by the inscribed \(\angle BAD\), so \(\angle BAD = \dfrac{1}{2}m(\text{arc } BCD)\) ...(1) (inscribed angle theorem). Arc BAD is intercepted by the inscribed \(\angle BCD\), so \(\angle BCD = \dfrac{1}{2}m(\text{arc } DAB)\) ...(2). Adding (1) and (2): \(\angle BAD + \angle BCD = \dfrac{1}{2}[m(\text{arc } BCD) + m(\text{arc } DAB)] = \dfrac{1}{2}\times 360^\circ = 180^\circ\). Since the sum of the measures of the angles of a quadrilateral is \(360^\circ\), \(\angle ADC + \angle ABC = 360^\circ - (\angle BAD + \angle BCD) = 360^\circ - 180^\circ = 180^\circ\). Hence the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.

stem: Eliminate \(\theta\), if \(x = 3\csc\theta + 4\cot\theta\) and \(y = 4\csc\theta - 3\cot\theta\).
solution: Let \(x = 3\csc\theta + 4\cot\theta\) ...(i) and \(y = 4\csc\theta - 3\cot\theta\) ...(ii). Multiplying (i) by 3 and (ii) by 4: \(3x = 9\csc\theta + 12\cot\theta\) and \(4y = 16\csc\theta - 12\cot\theta\). Adding these, \(3x + 4y = 25\csc\theta\), so \(\csc\theta = \dfrac{3x + 4y}{25}\). Multiplying (i) by 4 and (ii) by 3: \(4x = 12\csc\theta + 16\cot\theta\) and \(3y = 12\csc\theta - 9\cot\theta\). Subtracting, \(4x - 3y = 25\cot\theta\), so \(\cot\theta = \dfrac{4x - 3y}{25}\). Using \(\csc^2\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1\): \(\left(\dfrac{3x + 4y}{25}\right)^2 - \left(\dfrac{4x - 3y}{25}\right)^2 = 1\), i.e. \((3x + 4y)^2 - (4x - 3y)^2 = 625\).

stem: A toy is a combination of a cylinder, hemisphere and a cone, each with radius 10 cm as shown in the figure. Height of the conical part is 10 cm and total height is 60 cm. Find the total surface area of the toy. \((\pi = 3.14,\ \sqrt{2} = 1.41)\)
solution:
Radius \(r = 10\) cm (common to all three parts). Height of the conical part \(h = 10\) cm; height of the hemispherical part = its radius = 10 cm. So height of the cylindrical part \(h_1 = 60 - 10 - 10 = 40\) cm. Slant height of the cone: \(l^2 = r^2 + h^2 = 10^2 + 10^2 = 200\), so \(l = 10\sqrt{2} = 10\times 1.41 = 14.1\) cm.
Total surface area of the toy = curved surface area of the cone + curved surface area of the cylinder + curved surface area of the hemisphere \(= \pi r l + 2\pi r h_1 + 2\pi r^2 = \pi r(l + 2h_1 + 2r) = 3.14\times 10\,(14.1 + 2\times 40 + 2\times 10) = 31.4\times 114.1 = 3582.74\) cm\(^2\). Hence the total surface area of the toy is 3582.74 cm\(^2\).
figureNote: vertical composite toy: a cone on top, a cylinder in the middle, and a hemisphere at the bottom, each of radius 10 cm, p-03

stem: In the given figure, AD is the bisector of the exterior \(\angle A\) of \(\triangle ABC\). Seg AD intersects the side BC produced in D. Prove that \(\dfrac{BD}{CD} = \dfrac{AB}{AC}\).
solution:
Given: AD is the bisector of the exterior \(\angle A\) of \(\triangle ABC\) and intersects BC produced at D. Construction: Draw CE \(\parallel\) DA meeting AB at E.
Proof: Since CE \(\parallel\) DA, \(\angle 1 = \angle 3\) (alternate interior angles) and \(\angle 2 = \angle 4\) (corresponding angles, with BK a transversal). AD is the bisector of the exterior \(\angle A\), so \(\angle 1 = \angle 2\). Hence \(\angle 3 = \angle 4\), which gives \(AE = AC\) (sides opposite to equal angles are equal). By the Basic Proportionality Theorem (since EC \(\parallel\) AD in \(\triangle BAD\) with the transversal), \(\dfrac{BD}{CD} = \dfrac{AB}{EA}\). Since \(AE = AC\), \(\dfrac{BD}{CD} = \dfrac{AB}{AC}\).
figureNote: triangle ABC with vertex A at top and B, C on the base; side BC produced to D; ray AK is the bisector of the exterior angle at A; seg AD drawn to D, p-04

stem: Construct the circumcircle and incircle of an equilateral \(\triangle XYZ\) with side 6.5 cm and centre O. Find the ratio of the radii of the incircle and the circumcircle.
solution: Steps of construction: (1) Construct an equilateral \(\triangle XYZ\) with each side 6.5 cm. (2) Draw the perpendicular bisectors of any two sides; they meet at point O. (3) With centre O and radius OX, draw a circle — this is the circumcircle of \(\triangle XYZ\). (4) Draw the angle bisectors of any two angles (they also pass through O). (5) With centre O and radius equal to the perpendicular distance from O to a side, draw a circle — this is the incircle. For an equilateral triangle the incentre and circumcentre coincide, and the inradius \(r = \dfrac{R}{2}\), where \(R\) is the circumradius. Hence the ratio of the radii of the incircle to the circumcircle \(= 1 : 2\).

stem: A (5, 4), B (-3, -2) and C (1, -8) are the vertices of a triangle ABC. Find the equation of the median AD and the line parallel to AB passing through point C.
solution:
AD is the median on BC, so D is the midpoint of BC: \(D = \left(\dfrac{-3 + 1}{2},\ \dfrac{-2 + (-8)}{2}\right) = (-1, -5)\). Slope of AD: \(m_{AD} = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \dfrac{4 - (-5)}{5 - (-1)} = \dfrac{9}{6} = \dfrac{3}{2}\). Using \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) with A(5, 4): \(y - 4 = \dfrac{3}{2}(x - 5)\), i.e. \(2y - 8 = 3x - 15\), giving \(3x - 2y = 7\) — the required equation of median AD.
For the line parallel to AB, its slope equals the slope of AB \(= \dfrac{-2 - 4}{-3 - 5} = \dfrac{-6}{-8} = \dfrac{3}{4}\). Using \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) with C(1, -8): \(y - (-8) = \dfrac{3}{4}(x - 1)\), i.e. \(4y + 32 = 3x - 3\), giving \(3x - 4y = 35\) — the equation of the required line.
